newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican rebels declare election cease-fire.
newsitem.headline: Mexican rebels declare election cease-fire.

text.p: Marxist Mexican guerrillas have declared a temporary cease-fire in one central state to allow upcoming elections to go ahead without violence, media reported on Tuesday.
The self-styled Popular Revolutionary Army, known by its Spanish initials EPR, suspended all military offensives in the State of Mexico from midnight Tuesday local time (0600 GMT) to Nov. 17.

"We are looking to avoid that the federal and local government terrifies, uses violence or manipulates the popular participation of voters who want to exerice their right to vote voluntarily," an EPR communique said, La Jornada reported.
The State of Mexico, which almost completely surrounds Mexico City, votes on Sunday to elect 122 mayors and 75 state deputies.

It is one of the states where the EPR has been active since the first appearance of the shadowy guerrilla group in late June, vowing to topple the government of President Ernesto Zedillo. Clashes with police and military have left several dozen dead.
Rebels, operating in a handful of poverty-stricken central and southern states, called a similar cease-fire for recent elections in the state of Guerrero. The vote went ahead peacefully.

EPR activists called on State of Mexico residents to consider the elections there as a means of bringing democracy, justice and freedom to the state and called on them to vote to avoid fraud, La Jornada said.

"Electoral processes in the state ... have been characterised since their inception by the application of fraudulent government methods and by repression, applied to favor the ruling party for more than 60 years," La Jornada said citing the EPR communique.
"We are not opposed to elections, but we want them to be carried out openly and confidently so that the people can gain solutions to their problems," the guerrillas added.
